thread:
Ravi K.: Heads-up — self-serve reservation for 8x A100s in us-west-2 is stuck in the approval queue (request id r-2026-04-05-88). We need it for a canary rollout next week. Any way to bump priority?

Alice M.: Do you have the exact start/end window and billing commitment? That helps prioritize.

Ravi K.: Start Monday 04/12, 7 days initially. We asked for reserved because training+eval runs are heavy and we want predictable throughput.

Emma L.: Ticket shows long lead time for new reserved capacity in us-west-2 — avg fulfillment 6–12 days right now. Why reserved vs. burst?

Ravi K.: Reserved because runtime needs sustained throughput and we want pinning for the experiment. Burst would be too noisy for latency SLOs.

Jon P.: Tagging billing: reserving 8 A100s for 7 days will create a short-term reserved invoice line — we can convert to a commit/discount but need legal signoff if > $50k/mo. For 7d it's just pro-rated.

infra-bot: Reservation r-2026-04-05-88 status: queued -> pending-approval (ETA: 48h).

Ravi K.: 48h is risky. If queue slips we'll miss the canary. Can we escalate to dedicated pool or borrow from another region?

Alice M.: Options: 1) Cross-region fallback to us-east-1 or eu-west-1 with immediate availability, 2) Short-term spot/ephemeral burst in us-west-2 (higher jitter), 3) Manually allocate from reserved slack in prod pool (ops intervention + change window).

Emma L.: Cost/quality tradeoffs: cross-region adds ~30–60ms network egress and extra routing, might affect end-to-end latency tests. Spot will save cost but can preempt and break the experiment. Manual ops allocation is best signal, but reduces headroom for other customers.

Ravi K.: We care about tail latency — cross-region will invalidate the canary. Spot preemption is unacceptable. Please check manual ops allocation.

Alice M.: @Jon P. — if ops allocates from reserved slack, we need a temporary billing tag so cost shows against Ravi's project. Can you pre-create a cost tag and set an override?

Jon P.: I can create a temporary cost center tag `proj/canary-ravi-04-12` and backfill charges. Need an approval from infra-ops lead.

Emma L.: Quick sanity check: what's the minimal footprint? Can we run with 6x A100s for now to reduce impact on pool?

Ravi K.: 6 would slow experiments and push rollout. Would prefer 8 but can accept 6 for 48h if that prevents missing the window.

Alice M.: Two-stage plan: allocate 6 from reserved slack now (ops action), keep 2 in request queue to fulfill later. If queue fills earlier, we return slack. Ops window ~30 minutes.

infra-bot: Ops allocation request r-ops-456 created by Alice M. status: pending.

Alice M.: @oncall-team — would any scheduled maintenance block manual allocation in the next 2 hours?

Emma L.: Not that I see. No rolling upgrades until 03:00 UTC tonight.

Jon P.: Approval for cost tag received from finance (via email). I created `proj/canary-ravi-04-12`. Backfill will be applied.

Ravi K.: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Can we get a confirmation when the 6x allocation is live?

infra-bot: Allocation r-ops-456 completed. 6x A100s assigned to `proj/canary-ravi-04-12`.

Ravi K.: Confirmed. Machines are up. Running smoke tests now. :thumbsup:

Emma L.: I'll continue to monitor the original reservation queue. If the remaining 2 A100s get fulfilled we can add them as hot-swap.

Alice M.: Follow-up: let's capture this as a short-run playbook item — auto-fallback to ops-alloc + cost-tagging for customer-facing canaries. If we see this pattern again we should automate the approval path.

Ravi K.: Agreed. Logged a follow-up ticket for automation ideas.

Jon P.: One billing note — because we created short-term cost tagging and allocation outside normal reserved contract, we should track percent of reserved slack used monthly to not oversubscribe our commitments. I'll send a weekly digest.

Emma L.: I'll add a metric to the infra dashboard: "reserved-slack-utilization" and an alert if > 20% used by manual allocations.

Ravi K.: Thanks everyone. Can we close this thread once the canary completes?

Alice M.: Closing once rollback window passes. Good job moving quickly. :raised_hands:
